# Creek Freak Fantasy Football — Week 8 briefing
**As of Monday, October 26, 2026 | Tua in the pink | 12 teams | full PPR | 2 FLEX | head-to-head + weekly-median result**

## Executive call
**Your biggest problem is RB2, not WR.** Gibbs and McBride remain lineup anchors; Love has missed two games with an ankle injury, Montgomery has a groin injury and a Week 8 bye, and Roschon Johnson delivered only **1.3 PPR points** in Week 7. Prioritize a viable second RB and a one-week quarterback replacement for C.J. Stroud's Houston bye. Do **not** trade McBride at a discount just because your Week 7 flex decisions went badly.

**Three actions:** (1) activate/assess Jonah Coleman now that he has returned from IR; (2) add an available Week 8 QB — Malik Willis is my upside preference, Baker Mayfield my alternative — rather than relying on Bryce Young; (3) investigate Kimani Vidal and Dylan Sampson for RB depth. Confirm the Sleeper reserve-slot rules before submitting claims: Coleman remains in your reserve slot despite playing in Week 7, and an ineligible reserve designation may block roster moves.

## Your Week 7 review: the decisions that cost points
- **Trey McBride: 27.1 PPR**, 10 catches for 111 yards and a TD on 13 targets. Elite positional advantage; hold.
- **Jahmyr Gibbs: 17.3**, **C.J. Stroud: 16.52**; solid, not the problem.
- **Roschon Johnson: 1.3**, **Nico Collins: 2.6**, **Tetairoa McMillan: 8.0**, **Keenan Allen: 6.1**, **Germie Bernard: 5.7**. The RB2 slot and both FLEX spots cratered.
- **Bench: Jameson Williams 26.1 and Caleb Douglas 21.0.** The Allen-over-Jamo decision alone cost **20.0** points; Bernard-over-Jamo cost **20.4**. Do not overreact to one week, but the assumption that Allen/Bernard necessarily offered both a higher floor and higher ceiling was too strong.
- Douglas' 21 points came on **two catches, three targets, 70 yards and two TDs**. That's real big-play ability, **not** established weekly target volume. Hold as upside depth rather than instantly promoting him over every veteran.

The Week 7 NFL results back up the story: [McBride caught 10 for 111 and a TD](https://www.reuters.com/sports/nfl/bo-nix-throws-runs-tds-broncos-extend-cards-home-woes--flm-2026-10-25/), while [Douglas scored twice on three targets](https://www.fantasypros.com/nfl/news/615775/caleb-douglas-finds-end-zone-twice-week-7.php).

## Week 8 opponent and lineup outlook
**Opponent: Vicks Dogg Pound (6–6 in official standings).** Their preliminary Week 8 starters include Kyler Murray, Bijan Robinson, Jaylen Warren, Marvin Harrison Jr., Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland and T.J. Hockenson. This is a credible matchup; avoid giving away RB2 points.

**Week 8 schedule:** Panthers at Packers **Thursday Oct. 29**; most games **Sunday Nov. 1**; Bears at Seahawks **Monday Nov. 2**. **Houston, New Orleans, the Giants and San Francisco are on bye**. Source: [NFL Week 8 schedule](https://www.nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-8).

- **QB: STRONG NEED.** Stroud cannot play (Houston bye). Bryce Young just struggled in a 43–13 loss to Tampa Bay. Preferred available stream **Malik Willis (MIA vs NE)** for rushing upside and the Douglas stack; **Baker Mayfield (TB vs ATL)** is the alternate if his throwing thumb remains fine. Bo Nix (DEN vs KC) is a third choice after a big Week 7 rushing TD, but Kansas City is a much harder opponent. Justin Herbert (LAC vs LAR) is available too, but his 2026 offense and turnovers make him a less appealing immediate stream. [Willis Week 7](https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/malik-willis-accounts-for-3-tds-as-dolphins-beat-jets-for-first-win/); [Mayfield return](https://www.reuters.com/sports/nfl/buccaneers-rout-panthers-43-13-baker-mayfields-return--flm-2026-10-25/); [Herbert struggles](https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/players/2221960/justin-herbert/).
- **RB1 Gibbs: lock. RB2: urgent review.** Love (ARI at DAL) is a hold if he returns to practice, but has missed two straight games. **Jonah Coleman** returned for Denver and led the backfield with **nine carries, 54 rushing yards and two catches for 15**; he is on *your reserve list*, not the waiver wire. His Week 8 game against KC is a difficult three-way committee with Dobbins and RJ Harvey, but he merits consideration over Roschon if Love sits. **Montgomery has a Week 8 bye even if his groin improves.** [Love status](https://www.nbcsports.com/fantasy/football/player-news/2026-10-23/jeremiyah-love-ankle-ruled-out-vs-broncos); [Coleman usage](https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/players/28877250/jonah-coleman/); [Montgomery injury](https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/texans-david-montgomery-officially-ruled-out/).
- **WR:** Nico Collins also has a **Houston bye**, so he must leave the Week 8 starting lineup. Tetairoa McMillan plays Thursday at GB; Keenan Allen plays Jacksonville; Germie Bernard plays Cleveland; Jameson Williams faces Minnesota; Caleb Douglas faces New England. **Start Jamo ahead of Bernard for now**, pending practice/usage news; Douglas is a high-variance alternative, not a locked-in starter.
- **TE: McBride is an automatic start** at Dallas. **Denver D/ST vs Kansas City** is not a matchup to assume will be favorable; consider streaming after checking available defenses. The preliminary Week 8 Sleeper lineup is only a placeholder and still lists Stroud and Nico despite their bye.

They are not automatic claims; the key constraint is your RB2 availability, not collecting another TE or speculative WR. [Vidal usage](https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chargers-kimani-vidal-gets-10-touches-in-week-6-loss/); [Sampson Week 7](https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/browns-dylan-sampson-nine-touches-in-return/); [Sutton Week 7](https://www.fantasypros.com/nfl/news/615832/courtland-sutton-held-to-45-yards-week-7.php); [Dell return](https://nypost.com/2026/10/24/sports/tank-dell-returning-to-texans-for-first-time-in-nearly-two-years/).

**Drop/activation order:** First consider **Bryce Young** for a better Week 8 QB (Willis/Mayfield). For an RB add, **Roschon Johnson** is the first replaceable RB *if* Love is cleared and Coleman can be activated; otherwise protect enough startable RB bodies to fill two spots. Avoid dropping **Gibbs, Love, Coleman, Montgomery, Nico, Tetairoa, McBride, Jamo**. **Germie Bernard and Keenan Allen** remain holdable depth but are trade/roster-churn candidates if their target roles shrink. **Jordyn Tyson** is on reserve with an IR designation; keep him there unless league rules force a change. Check reserve eligibility: Coleman played Sunday and may need moving to an active roster slot before waiver adds can process.

## Trade board — targets actually rostered in Creek Freak
**Strong strategy: convert WR surplus into a reliable RB2; do not panic-sell McBride.** Trade deadline is configured for **Week 11**, so there is a limited window.

1. **Approach 2 Girls 1 Kupp (Lincoln)** about **Rhamondre Stevenson** (also has Kyren Williams and Javonte Williams). They currently project **Malik Washington** in a flex slot and have Puka/Garrett Wilson at WR. Explore **Jameson Williams for Stevenson**, with minor adjustments only if needed. This is a negotiation starting point, not a fair-value guarantee; Stevenson has workload value but some knee/receiving volatility. **Kyren or Javonte would require a materially stronger offer.**
2. **Approach Landry Kiffin** about **Chuba Hubbard** (also has RJ Harvey and Woody Marks). Landry's provisional WR starters are CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith, and the team is 6–6. A package led by **Tetairoa McMillan plus another useful WR** might start a conversation for Chuba, but his strong 2026 workload means this is **exploratory, not a cheap buy-low**. RJ Harvey is less attractive as an RB2 now that Coleman has re-entered Denver's three-man committee.
3. **Trey McBride sell-high: only for a clear RB upgrade plus an acceptable TE replacement.** His 27.1-point Week 7 is real leverage, but the rest of your roster has enough WR depth to shop there first. Do not swap McBride for a middling RB or for a receiver-only package.

**Sell-high caution:** Caleb Douglas' two-touchdown, three-target Week 7 is a chance to test interest, **not** proof he is now a volume WR1. **Buy-low caution:** Montgomery is hurt and on bye; offers will reflect that. Prefer holding until his return unless you get meaningful usable RB value.

## Injury and usage watch through Thursday
- **Jeremiyah Love (ankle):** missed Weeks 6 and 7; monitor Wednesday/Thursday practice and Arizona's Thursday-to-Sunday reporting. His Week 8 status dictates whether Coleman or a waiver RB starts.
- **David Montgomery (groin):** missed Week 7; Texans bye Week 8 gives recovery time, but no Week 8 fantasy points. [Status](https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/texans-david-montgomery-officially-ruled-out/).
- **Jonah Coleman:** returned from IR and led Denver with nine carries; [Sean Payton wants more touches](https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/players/28877250/jonah-coleman/). Watch whether the committee consolidates.
- **Nico Collins:** Week 8 bye. Hold rather than treating his 2.6-point Week 7 as a reason to sell cheaply.
- **Jameson Williams vs Germie Bernard:** Jamo's 26.1 on your bench was painful; Bernard's Week 6 12 targets (and 21 over two weeks) were legitimate reasons to consider him, but Week 7's 5.7 reminds us that target projections are not guarantees. Track routes/targets again.
- **Malik Willis + Caleb Douglas:** Willis had **208 passing yards, two passing TDs and 37 rushing yards with a rushing score**; Douglas had two TDs on three targets. Watch whether Douglas's target share grows against New England. [Game report](https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/malik-willis-accounts-for-3-tds-as-dolphins-beat-jets-for-first-win/).
- **Jalen Hurts:** now expected out for the season. Do not waste a claim re-adding him simply because he appears in the available-player list. [Report](https://www.reuters.com/sports/nfl-nflpa-handling-joint-review-jalen-hurts-diagnosis--flm-2026-10-25/).

## Action plan / decision rules
1. **Today:** check whether the healthy Coleman occupying a reserve slot prevents claims. If so, activate him; prioritize removing a fringe bench piece rather than sacrificing core WR/RB value.
2. **Before waivers:** target **Willis** (QB streamer) and **Vidal or Sampson** (RB depth), using Bryce Young and/or Roschon as the most plausible roster churn. If you can add only one, weigh whether Love is practicing: **RB if Love remains out; QB if you otherwise must start Bryce**.
3. **Before Thursday Oct. 29:** make the QB decision and lock in Tetairoa only if you want him against Green Bay; verify injury statuses.
4. **Sunday Nov. 1:** play Gibbs/McBride, remove Houston players on bye, reassess Love vs Coleman vs new RB. Lean Jamo over Bernard in the flex pending new target evidence.
5. **Trades:** send targeted RB inquiries to Lincoln and Landry, but avoid two-for-one overpays just to win Week 8.

**Bottom line:** You're still officially first in the last finalized standings, but your provisional Week 7 loss highlights the real issue: an injury-thinned RB room and too many volatile FLEX decisions. Make an RB2 plan, stream the Houston-bye QB slot, and preserve your elite Gibbs–McBride foundation.

*Data notes: League rosters, player availability, transactions, standings and scores are from the connected Sleeper league read on Oct. 26, 2026. The Week 7 scoreboard is provisional. Player usage/injury context is from linked contemporary reports. No waivers or trades were submitted.*
